# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III of the EU AI Act has changed. The original Regulation 2024/1689 set **2 August 2026** as the date these rules would take effect (high confidence), but a political agreement reached on 7 May 2026 and the subsequent "AI Omnibus" amendment—which entered into force on **27 July 2026**—extended this date, with legal analysis placing it at **2 December 2027** (high confidence on the extension itself; medium confidence on the specific statutory date, since this figure derives from secondary legal analysis rather than an explicit quote in the EUR-Lex consolidated text). Many secondary sources have not yet been updated to reflect this change, creating significant confusion in public-facing guidance.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Regulation 2024/1689, as originally adopted, specified that rules governing high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Date
Following political agreement on 7 May 2026, the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI) extended the Annex III application date, with the European Commission's own FAQ and news page stating the new date is 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([European Commission FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus Enters Into Force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

However, the exact statutory mapping of this date is less firmly established than it first appears. The consolidated EUR-Lex text, applicable from 27 July 2026, replaces the original fixed 2 August 2026 date with a generic reference to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" (high confidence), but it does not itself spell out that this date is 2 December 2027 ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). The specific 2 December 2027 figure comes from independent legal analysis of amended Article 113(c)(i), which concludes that Chapter III Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III obligations, except Article 6(5)) apply from that date—this mapping is assessed at medium confidence given it is not directly quoted in the primary legal text ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). In other words, the 7 May 2026 political agreement and 27 July 2026 entry into force are well-documented (high confidence), but the precise resulting application date relies on secondary interpretation of the amended Article 113 rather than an explicit EUR-Lex statement.

### Rationale for the Delay
The European Commission had proposed adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, conditioning application on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools would be available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The delay was driven by the slow development of harmonised technical standards needed to give providers and enforcers legal certainty (medium confidence) ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Related Deadlines
Under the amended timeline, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([European Commission FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [LinkedIn - Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). High-risk systems already on the market or in service before the Chapter III application date remain subject to the Regulation only if they undergo significant design changes afterward, though public-authority deployers/providers must act regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources are sharply split between the original 2 August 2026 date and the amended 2 December 2027 date, largely reflecting whether a source was updated after the 27 July 2026 omnibus entry into force ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [EC Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). One source gives 2 August 2027 for Annex I product-embedded systems, conflicting with the 2028 date cited elsewhere (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). Some commentary treats "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" as the binding citation for the omnibus; this is flagged as low confidence since it appears only in secondary sources, not in primary EU materials ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)). An earlier general description citing a 36-month post-entry-into-force timeline (~August 2027) does not match either specific date and may reflect imprecision (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether all Chapter III, Sections 1–3 provisions are uniformly delayed to 2 December 2027, or if sub-provisions like Article 6(5) retain separate dates. The official EUR-Lex text does not explicitly state the new date, leaving ambiguity about exact statutory language pending further confirmation or a clarified consolidated version. The correct final citation for the omnibus regulation is unconfirmed in primary sources. Enforcement consequences if standards remain unfinished by December 2027 are not addressed in available sources.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III of the EU AI Act has changed. The original Regulation 2024/1689 set **2 August 2026** as the date these rules would take effect (high confidence), but a political agreement reached on 7 May 2026 and the subsequent "AI Omnibus" amendment—which entered into force on **27 July 2026**—pushed this date to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). Many secondary sources have not yet been updated to reflect this change, creating significant confusion in public-facing guidance.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Regulation 2024/1689, as originally adopted, specified that rules governing high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Date
Following political agreement on 7 May 2026, the "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI) extended the Annex III application date to 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([European Commission FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [AI Omnibus Enters Into Force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). The consolidated EUR-Lex text, applicable from that date, reflects a revised "date of application of Chapter III" rather than the original fixed 2 August 2026 date (high confidence), though it refers to this generically via Article 113 rather than quoting 2 December 2027 explicitly ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Legal analysis of amended Article 113(c)(i) similarly concludes that Chapter III Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III obligations, except Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) ([AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### Rationale for the Delay
The European Commission had proposed adjusting the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months, conditioning application on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools would be available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The delay was driven by the slow development of harmonised technical standards needed to give providers and enforcers legal certainty (medium confidence) ([Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Related Deadlines
Under the amended timeline, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([European Commission FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [LinkedIn - Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). High-risk systems already on the market or in service before the Chapter III application date remain subject to the Regulation only if they undergo significant design changes afterward, though public-authority deployers/providers must act regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources are sharply split between the original 2 August 2026 date and the amended 2 December 2027 date, largely reflecting whether a source was updated after the 27 July 2026 omnibus entry into force ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [EC Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). One source gives 2 August 2027 for Annex I product-embedded systems, conflicting with the 2028 date cited elsewhere (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)). Some commentary treats "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" as the binding citation for the omnibus, but this flagged as low confidence since it appears only in secondary sources ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)). An earlier general description citing a 36-month post-entry-into-force timeline (~August 2027) does not match either specific date and may reflect imprecision (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether all Chapter III, Sections 1–3 provisions are uniformly delayed to 2 December 2027, or if sub-provisions like Article 6(5) retain separate dates. The official EUR-Lex text does not explicitly state the new date, leaving some ambiguity about exact statutory language. The correct final citation for the omnibus regulation is unconfirmed in primary sources. Enforcement consequences if standards remain unfinished by December 2027 are not addressed in available sources.
